subject.title: Gateway silently skips channel initialization on plugin/runtime mismatch or missing module files

question: What startup contract should OpenClaw use when a configured channel plugin is incompatible, absent before registration, or unhealthy during owner setup?
rationale: The issue spans fail-fast versus warn-and-continue behavior, audit output shape, plugin metadata lifecycle, owner-plugin health checks, and performance caching, so an automated repair should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Warn-and-continue with channel audit
options.body: Add a startup/readiness audit that names configured, attempted, loaded, and failed channels with reasons, while routing repair and reload through doctor/status or an explicit owner reload flow.

options.title: Fail fast for configured channel blockers
options.body: Treat configured channel incompatibility or missing owner modules as startup-blocking errors, accepting a sharper failure mode for existing installs.

options.title: Keep partial diagnostics only
options.body: Leave plugin discovery warnings, missing-module hints, and configured-channel warnings as the supported diagnostics, and split remaining requests into narrower owner/plugin issues.

recommendation.title: Warn-and-continue with channel audit
recommendation.body: Add a startup/readiness audit that names configured, attempted, loaded, and failed channels with reasons, while routing repair and reload through doctor/status or an explicit owner reload flow.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is mostly about plugin/channel ownership boundaries and startup policy, where this account has the strongest related history signal from current files and prior review discussion.
